newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge stock up on Japan deal.
newsitem.headline: Newbridge stock up on Japan deal.

text.p: Shares in Newbridge Networks Corp rose in New York and Toronto on Thursday after the company signed a long-awaited supply deal with Japan's Matsushita Communication Industrial Co.
Newbridge said in a statement that the deal, anticipated for months by industry analysts, was the largest it has ever won in Japan.
The length of the supply contract and its estimated value were not disclosed because of confidentiality agreements with Matsushita, said Newbridge spokesman Paul Goyette.

Analysts have said the value of the deal depends on the progress of deregulation in Japan. Goyette said other deals involving telecommunications carriers and large corporations are still possible and would be announced separately. "There's always the potential of additional business," he said.

Newbridge will supply Matsushita with VIVID switched multimedia routing equipment for local area network (LAN) applications, the MainStreet line of time division multiplexer and frame relay systems and the 46020 MainStreet network manager and associated equipment for original equipment manufacturer (OEM) distribution in Japan.

Matsushita will initially deliver the Newbridge products to domestic carrier networks such as those of Nippon Telephone and Telegraph as well as to financial institutions, corporations and government organizations.

Newbridge said possible applications for this equipment include airport systems, transportation systems, large corporate backbones, campus LAN backbones, Internet services, global wide area networks (WANs), research and development networks, interactive distance learning, medical imaging and videoconferencing.
The company cited forecasts which estimate that the market opportunity in Japan for local and wide area networking products could hit US$4 billion a year by the year 2000.
Newbridge shares rose 2.85 in active trading on the TSE to 85.65 and added 2 to 62-3/8 on Wall Street.
The company's annual meeting will be held today in Ottawa.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
